The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondent under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 10.10.2019 2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That, on 10.10.2019 at about 7.00 a.m., while the petitioner was traveling as a driver in the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-F-1628 on Maithani Alageri Village,
Thirthahalli, Shivamogga, at that time the driver of said KSRTC Bus drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, thereby lost control over the bus and turtle the bus on left side of the road.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous SCCH-10 injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to NH Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality hospital,
Shivamogga and after first aid, he was admitted as an inpatient from 10.10.2019 to 14.10.2019.

entities.text:
NH Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality hospital,
Shivamogga
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
He spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, hospitalization, food,
nourishment and other incidental charges and as per the advice of the doctors, he continued treatment and underwent physiotherapy.
Again he admitted to the Hosmat hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 19.01.2020 to 21.01.2020 and underwent surgery.
As per the advice of the doctor, he is still taking follow-up treatment.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, he was working as a KSRTC Bus driver and earning a sum of Rs.12,400/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner has suffered disability and he is unable to do his work as he was doing earlier.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 07-F-1628.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to award SCCH-10 compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- under various heads with interest and costs.
3. In pursuance of notice, the respondent has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

4. The brief contentions of the respondent are as under:
The respondent contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

The respondent has denied the Gopal vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162277611/
2 accident, manner of accident and rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-F-1628.

sentences.text: It is contended that, the petitioner was deputed as Driver in the offending bus in schedule No.74/75 and the petitioner has permitted the conductor unauthorizedly to drive the offending bus on the date of accident.
Hence, the petitioner/driver himself is negligent for cause of alleged accident.
Further contended that, the petitioner even after the accident continued his job.
The medical bills were reimbursed by the corporation.
SCCH-10
Further, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

On these grounds, respondent prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.
5.

On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 10.10.2019 at about 7.00 a.m., while the petitioner was traveling in the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-F-1628 on Maithani Alageri Village, Thirthahalli, Shivamogga, at that time, the driver of said KSRTC Bus drove the same with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
thereby lost control over the said bus and turtle on the left side of the road.
As a result petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injury ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
6. The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.

On the other hand, the respondent has examined SCCH-10 Asst. Traffic Superintendent as RW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5.
7.
Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

8. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :
R E A S O N S 9.

ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 10.10.2019 10.

According to the petitioner, while he traveling as a driver in the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.
No.KA-07-F-1628 on Maithani Alageri Village, Thirthahalli, Shivamogga, at that time the driver of said KSRTC Bus drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, thereby lost control over the bus and turtle the bus on left side of the road and SCCH-10 due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

11. To substantiate the said contentions, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
12.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of the First Information statement and Ex.P.3 is the Charge sheet filed by the of Agumbe Police.

On perusal of Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.3, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC against one Mr. Venkatesh Babu, who was the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 07-F-1628 on the date of accident.
Further, as per the wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.4, it appears that the petitioner has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.

13. The respondent in the written statement has specifically contended that, the driver who was driving the vehicle on the date of accident by name Mr. Venkatesh Babu was deputed as conductor to the said vehicle and the SCCH-10 petitioner has unauthorizedly allowed the conductor to drive the vehicle and hence, due to the negligent act of the petitioner the accident occurred.
14.
The respondent has examined its Asst. Traffic Superintendent as RW-1.
He has reiterated the contents of the written statement in his examination-in-chief.

During the cross-examination of RW1,
he has admitted that on the date of accident said Venkatesh Babu was deputed as driver cum conductor to the said KSRTC bus.
Since said Venkatesh Babu deputed as Conductor cum driver, it appears that he is authorized to drive the bus as an alternative driver during the absence of regular driver.
Further, as per the police records it reveal that, at the time of accident said Venkatesh Babu was driving the vehicle in a rash and manner and caused the accident.

Therefore, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries due to the accident.

15. Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and SCCH-10 the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-F-1628.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

16. ISSUE No.2 :-
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

The petitioner contended that, due to the accident he has suffered grievous injuries and taken treatment at Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality hospital, Shivamogga as an inpatient and spent more that Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment and he has also admitted to Hosmat hospital and under went surgery.
18.

entities.text: Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality hospital, Shivamogga
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In support of his contention, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate issued by Sahyadri Narayana Multi Speciality hospital.

Except said wound certificate and SCCH-10 the oral evidence, the petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence to show that he was admitted to the hospitals, taken treatment as inpatient and spent several lakhs towards medical expenses.

It is also significant to note that, the petitioner neither examined the doctor who treated the petitioner nor produced any disability certificate to show that, due to the accident he is permanently disabled.
19. The respondent in the written statement has specifically denied the expenses incurred by the petitioner towards hospitalization and other expenses as stated by the petitioner.

20. During the cross-examination of PW-1 he admitted as under;
"Hosmat

." 
From the very admission of PW-1 clearly establishes that, the respondent corporation has reimbursed the medical expenses spent by the petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

RW-1 during his chief examination has produced the advance / deposit register which were marked as Ex.R.2 and Ex.R.3 wherein it clearly establish that, the respondent has paid the medical expenses of Rs.86,278/- and Rs.80,000/- respectively.

21. As stated supra, in the instant case, the petitioner has not produced any document i.e. medical records as well as medical bills to establish that, he has spent several lakhs towards medical expenses.

On the other hand, the admission of PW-1 as well as the document produced by the respondent clearly establish that, the respondent have already paid the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not entitled for SCCH-10 any compensation under the head medical expenses.

22. However, considering the injuries suffered by the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospitals as an inpatient, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, if Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded Gopal vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162277611/
5 under the heads of pain and sufferings it will be just and proper.

23. LIABILITY:
As far as liability is concerned, the respondent who is the owner cum internal insurer of the offending KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-07-F-1628 is liable to pay Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. to the petitioner from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section SCCH-10 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
After deposit, entire compensation amount shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-
Draw award accordingly.
